label: Ricotta forte
note: Fermented by bacteria and yeast, like Greek kopanisti

about.text: Ricotta forte is a traditional soft, creamy, spicy and slightly bitter cheese of Basilicata and Apulia in southern Italy. Bacteria and yeast ferment the ricotta, which gives it its sharp taste and strong smell. It is on the Italian list of traditional food products (PAT).

steps.name: salt
steps.note: About 20 g per kg is mixed in right after the ricotta is lifted out.

steps.name: stir
steps.note: Stirred smooth with a long wooden spoon.
Turned on alternate days to stop mould.

processing.text: Salted whey ricotta fermented in terracotta or plastic containers; no species named. Sources give 2 to 6 months, 5 months, or 60 days to years.
